# 1 Maccabees Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 9 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

This chapter narrates the death of Judas Maccabeus and the rise of his brother Jonathan. The lament of v.21 — "How has the mighty fallen, the savior of Israel!" — deliberately echoes David's lament over Saul and Jonathan in 2 Samuel 1:25-27, signaling Judas's heroic stature. The chapter then traces the difficult, often desperate early leadership of Jonathan, culminating in his settlement at Michmash and the pacification of the land.

**Key term rulings:**
- "slipped away" (v.6) — preferred over "deserted" to preserve the Greek's flavor of gradual dispersal
- "crushed in spirit" (v.7) — literal rendering of the Greek; conveys psychological weight
- "Far be it from me" (v.10) — classic biblical idiom; retained
- "Savior of Israel" (v.21) — capitalized given the messianic resonance
- "workers of iniquity" (v.23) — biblical register appropriate to the narrative's Samuel-Kings style
- "a prophet ceased to appear" (v.27) — indicates the end of the prophetic era; significant theological note
- "lords of the country" (v.25) — preferred over "rulers" to mark the illegitimacy of Bacchides' appointments

---

**1** When Demetrius heard that Nicanor had fallen with his forces in battle, he sent Bacchides and Alcimus back into the land of Judah a second time, with the right wing of his army.

**2** They marched by the road leading to Gilgal and encamped against Mesaloth in Arbela; they captured it and killed many people.

**3** In the first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year they encamped against Jerusalem.

**4** They set out and marched to Berea with twenty thousand infantry and two thousand cavalry.

**5** Judas was encamped at Elasa with three thousand picked men.

**6** When they saw the size of the enemy force, they were badly frightened, and many slipped away from the camp until only eight hundred men remained.

**7** Judas saw that his army had slipped away and that the battle pressed upon him; he was crushed in spirit, for he had no time to gather them.

**8** Yet he gathered himself and said to those remaining: "Let us rise up and go against our enemies; perhaps we can still fight them."

**9** But they urged him back: "We cannot. Let us save our lives now and return with our brothers, and then fight them; we are too few."

**10** Judas replied: "Far be it from me to do such a thing as to flee from them. If our time has come, let us die bravely for our brothers and leave no reproach against our honor."

**11** The enemy army moved out of camp and took its position to meet them. The cavalry split into two wings; slingers and archers marched before the army; the most powerful warriors held the front.

**12** Bacchides was stationed on the right flank. The phalanx advanced on both sides to the sound of the trumpets.

**13** The men of Judas also blew their trumpets, and the earth shook from the noise of the armies; the battle raged from morning until evening.

**14** Judas saw that Bacchides and the strength of his army were positioned on the right, and all the courageous rallied around him.

**15** The right wing was broken, and he pursued them to the slope of Azotus.

**16** Those on the left wing, seeing the right had been broken, turned and followed the tracks of Judas and his men from the rear.

**17** The battle grew fierce; many fell on both sides.

**18** Then Judas fell, and the rest fled.

**19** Jonathan and Simon took their brother Judas and buried him in the tomb of their ancestors at Modein.

**20** They wept for him. All Israel made great lamentation and mourned for him for many days, saying:

**21** "How has the mighty fallen, the Savior of Israel!"

**22** The remaining acts of Judas — his wars, his brave deeds, and his greatness — were not recorded, for they were very many.

**23** After the death of Judas, the lawless raised their heads throughout all the territory of Israel, and all the workers of iniquity emerged again.

**24** In those days a very great famine struck, and the land went over to their side with them.

**25** Bacchides deliberately chose renegade men and appointed them lords of the land.

**26** They sought out and hunted down the friends of Judas and brought them to Bacchides, who took vengeance on them and treated them harshly.

**27** It was a great tribulation in Israel, the like of which had not been since the time a prophet ceased to appear among them.

**28** Then all the friends of Judas assembled and said to Jonathan:

**29** "Since your brother Judas died, there has been no one like him to go against our enemies and against Bacchides and against those who hate our nation.

**30** Now therefore we have chosen you today to be our ruler and leader in his place, to fight our battles."

**31** Jonathan accepted the leadership at that time and took the place of his brother Judas.

**32** When Bacchides learned of this, he sought to kill him.

**33** Jonathan and his brother Simon and all those with them learned of it and fled into the wilderness of Tekoa, encamping beside the pool of Asphar.

**34** Bacchides learned of this on the Sabbath and crossed the Jordan with all his forces.

**35** Jonathan had sent his brother John ahead as leader of the people to request that the Nabateans, their friends, take custody of a large amount of baggage.

**36** But the sons of Jambri came out from Medaba, seized John, and made off with everything he had.

**37** After these things, word came to Jonathan and Simon that the sons of Jambri were celebrating a great wedding and escorting the bride from Nadabath — daughter of one of the great nobles of Canaan — with a large retinue.

**38** They remembered the blood of John their brother, and went up and hid under cover of the mountainside.

**39** They looked and saw a noisy procession with much baggage; the bridegroom came out with his friends and brothers to meet them, with tambourines and musicians and many weapons.

**40** They rose up from their ambush and struck them down; many fell, and the rest fled into the hills. The Jews took all their spoils.

**41** The wedding was turned to mourning and the voice of their music to lamentation.

**42** They had avenged the blood of their brother, and returned to the marshes of the Jordan.

**43** When Bacchides heard, he came on the Sabbath to the banks of the Jordan with a great force.

**44** Jonathan said to his men: "Rise up and let us fight for our lives. Today is not like yesterday or before.

**45** For see, the battle is in front and behind us; the Jordan waters us on this side and on that, with marsh and thicket — there is nowhere to turn.

**46** Now cry out to Heaven, that you may be saved from your enemies."

**47** The battle was joined; Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, but Bacchides drew back from him.

**48** Jonathan and his men leaped into the Jordan and swam across to the other side; the enemy did not cross after them.

**49** About one thousand of Bacchides' men fell that day.

**50** Bacchides returned to Jerusalem and built strongly fortified cities in Judea: at Jericho, Emmaus, Beth-horon, Bethel, Timnath, Pharathon, and Tephon — with high walls, gates, and bars.

**51** He stationed garrisons in them to harass Israel.

**52** He also fortified Beth-zur, Gazara, and the citadel, placing troops and stores of food in them.

**53** He took the sons of the leading men of the land as hostages and placed them under guard in the citadel in Jerusalem.

**54** In the one hundred and fifty-third year, in the second month, Alcimus gave orders to tear down the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary — destroying the work of the prophets. He had begun to tear it down

**55** when Alcimus was struck down; his work was stopped, and his mouth was sealed. He was paralyzed and could speak no word nor give orders for his own household.

**56** Alcimus died at that time in great suffering.

**57** When Bacchides saw that Alcimus was dead, he returned to the king. The land of Judah was at rest for two years.

**58** Then all the lawless consulted together: "Jonathan and his men are dwelling in safety and confidence. Let us bring Bacchides now, and he will seize them all in a single night."

**59** They went and consulted with him.

**60** He set out with a large force and sent secret letters to all his allies in Judea to seize Jonathan and those with him. But they were unable to do it, for the plot became known to Jonathan.

**61** Jonathan and his men seized about fifty of the local ringleaders of the scheme and killed them.

**62** Then Jonathan and Simon and their companions withdrew to Bethbasi in the wilderness; they rebuilt its ruins and made it strong.

**63** When Bacchides heard, he gathered his whole force and sent orders to his contacts in Judea.

**64** He came and besieged Bethbasi, fighting against it for many days and building siege machines.

**65** Jonathan left Simon his brother in the city and slipped out into the countryside with a select force.

**66** He struck down Odomera and his brothers and the sons of Phaseron in their tents, and they began striking down and advancing through the forces.

**67** Simon and his men sortied from the city and burned the siege machines.

**68** They fought against Bacchides and crushed him; they harassed him severely, for his plan and all his campaign came to nothing.

**69** He was greatly angered with the lawless men who had counseled him to come into the land, and he killed many of them; then he resolved to return to his own land.

**70** When Jonathan learned of this, he sent envoys to make peace and to secure the release of prisoners.

**71** Bacchides accepted gladly and acted on Jonathan's terms, swearing under oath to do him no harm for the rest of his life.

**72** He handed over the prisoners he had previously taken in the land of Judah, then turned and went back to his own land, never to enter their territory again.

**73** Thus the sword ceased from Israel. Jonathan settled at Michmash and began to judge the people, and he exterminated the godless from Israel.
